description: A low, stiff, spiny shrub 0.5-1.5 m tall whose stems carry three sharp spines at every node, with small round lobed leaves, hanging dark red and white flowers like little fuchsias in spring, and round red berries covered in prickles in summer. It grows on dry, rocky slopes in chaparral, foothill pine and oak woodland and up into the pine belt, where bears, foxes, coyotes, jays and quail eat its berries and quail and rabbits shelter under its spines.

season_notes.winter: Bare, stiff grey-brown stems bristling with spines in threes.
season_notes.spring: Small lobed leaves unfold in March, and dark red flowers with white tips hang under the stems like tiny fuchsias, March to May; hummingbirds and bees visit.
season_notes.summer: Round spiny berries ripen from green to red and purple-red, June to August; in the dry heat the leaves begin to yellow and fall.
season_notes.fall: Mostly bare already, a few leaves left, red to orange.

notes: Sierra gooseberry is a deciduous shrub 0.5-1.5 m of dry, open, often rocky slopes in chaparral, foothill pine and oak woodland and the mixed conifer belt, common through the Sierra foothills. Form: plain 'shrub'. Four to seven stiff stems from the base (stems [4, 7]) spread widely (stem_spread 54) with side shoots held out nearly level (level-1 down angle 58 at the base, 45 at the top); the stiff, angular look comes from zigzag_deg on both levels and the twigs (a bend at each node where a spine cluster and a short shoot sit) rather than from curvature. Three stout spines at each node and bristles on the young stems (not modelled; a card cannot carry them). Bark grey to red-brown, shredding on old stems (bark_pattern shreddy); twig_rgb is the paler grey-tan of the spiny young shoots. Leaves alternate or clustered on short shoots, round, 1-3 cm, three- to five-lobed and toothed, softly hairy: leaf_shape lobed, leaf_size_m 0.02. Flowers 1-2 at a node, hanging, with dark red to purple-red reflexed sepals and white petals, like small fuchsias, March to May with the new leaves (before_leaves false): form bud, rgb a dark red-purple. Berries round, about 1-1.5 cm, densely covered in prickles, red to purple-red, June to August: form bud. Drought- and winter-deciduous: in the long dry summer the leaves yellow and drop from August, a few hang on into October, and the shrub is bare December to February (leaf_on_by_month). Ribes are alternate hosts of white pine blister rust, which matters to sugar pines in the conifer belt above. Architectural model provisional.
